#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install.sh — install harness skills and context files at the user level
#
# Usage:
#   ./install.sh                          # default install into ~/.claude
#   ./install.sh --dir <path>             # alternate Claude Code dir (testing)
#   ./install.sh --with <skill>           # also install an optional skill
#                                         # (repeatable; e.g. --with next-react-boot)
#   ./install.sh --with all               # install every optional skill
#
# Skills land in <claude-dir>/skills/ and context files land in
# <claude-dir>/AGENTS.md and <claude-dir>/CLAUDE.md, so they apply to every
# project automatically.
#
# Optional skills are project bootstraps that only make sense in specific
# stacks. They are skipped by default. Request them explicitly with --with.

set -euo pipefail

HARNESS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── optional skills ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Skipped by default; opt in with --with <name>.
OPTIONAL_SKILLS=(next-react-boot python-psql-boot)

# ── arg parsing ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
USER_CLAUDE_DIR="$HOME/.claude"
REQUESTED_OPTIONAL=()

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dir)
      USER_CLAUDE_DIR="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --with)
      if [[ "$2" == "all" ]]; then
        REQUESTED_OPTIONAL=("${OPTIONAL_SKILLS[@]}")
      else
        REQUESTED_OPTIONAL+=("$2")
      fi
      shift 2
      ;;
    -h|--help)
      sed -n '2,16p' "$0"
      exit 0
      ;;
    *)
      printf 'unknown argument: %s\n' "$1" >&2
      printf 'see ./install.sh --help\n' >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
done

mkdir -p "$USER_CLAUDE_DIR"
USER_CLAUDE_DIR="$(cd "$USER_CLAUDE_DIR" && pwd)"
SKILLS_SRC="$HARNESS_DIR/skills"
SKILLS_DST="$USER_CLAUDE_DIR/skills"

# Validate any requested optional skills actually exist on disk.
for req in "${REQUESTED_OPTIONAL[@]+"${REQUESTED_OPTIONAL[@]}"}"; do
  if [[ ! -d "$SKILLS_SRC/$req" ]]; then
    printf 'requested optional skill not found: %s\n' "$req" >&2
    printf 'available optional skills: %s\n' "${OPTIONAL_SKILLS[*]}" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

# Helper: is this skill name an optional one?
is_optional() {
  local name="$1"
  local s
  for s in "${OPTIONAL_SKILLS[@]}"; do
    [[ "$s" == "$name" ]] && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

# Helper: was this optional skill requested?
is_requested() {
  local name="$1"
  local s
  for s in "${REQUESTED_OPTIONAL[@]+"${REQUESTED_OPTIONAL[@]}"}"; do
    [[ "$s" == "$name" ]] && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

# ── helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

green()  { printf '\033[32m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
yellow() { printf '\033[33m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
bold()   { printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }

# ── 1. copy skills ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

mkdir -p "$SKILLS_DST"

installed=()
updated=()
skipped=()

for skill_dir in "$SKILLS_SRC"/*/; do
  skill_name="$(basename "$skill_dir")"
  dst="$SKILLS_DST/$skill_name"

  if is_optional "$skill_name" && ! is_requested "$skill_name"; then
    skipped+=("$skill_name")
    continue
  fi

  if [[ -d "$dst" ]]; then
    rm -rf "$dst"
    cp -r "$skill_dir" "$dst"
    updated+=("$skill_name")
  else
    cp -r "$skill_dir" "$dst"
    installed+=("$skill_name")
  fi
done

# Prune skills that no longer exist in the harness source (handles renames + removals).
# An optional skill that wasn't requested is NOT pruned — it still exists in the source,
# so only genuinely deleted/renamed skills are removed.
removed=()
if [[ -d "$SKILLS_DST" ]]; then
  for dst_dir in "$SKILLS_DST"/*/; do
    [[ -d "$dst_dir" ]] || continue
    dst_name="$(basename "$dst_dir")"
    if [[ ! -d "$SKILLS_SRC/$dst_name" ]]; then
      rm -rf "$dst_dir"
      removed+=("$dst_name")
    fi
  done
fi

bold "Skills → $SKILLS_DST"
for s in "${installed[@]+"${installed[@]}"}"; do green  "  + $s"; done
for s in "${updated[@]+"${updated[@]}"}";    do yellow "  ↺ $s"; done
for s in "${removed[@]+"${removed[@]}"}";    do printf '  - %s (removed — no longer in harness)\n' "$s"; done
for s in "${skipped[@]+"${skipped[@]}"}";    do printf '  · %s (optional — request with --with %s)\n' "$s" "$s"; done

# ── 2. context files (AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md) ─────────────────────────────────

HARNESS_REL="$(python3 -c "import os; print(os.path.relpath('$HARNESS_DIR', '$USER_CLAUDE_DIR'))" 2>/dev/null || echo "$HARNESS_DIR")"

skills_table() {
  cat <<EOF
| Skill | Invoke | SKILL.md |
|---|---|---|
| initialize | \`/initialize\` | [→]($HARNESS_REL/skills/initialize/SKILL.md) |
| problem-spec | \`/problem-spec\` | [→]($HARNESS_REL/skills/problem-spec/SKILL.md) |
| plan | \`/plan\` | [→]($HARNESS_REL/skills/plan/SKILL.md) |
| verify | \`/verify\` | [→]($HARNESS_REL/skills/verify/SKILL.md) |
| clean-code | \`/clean-code\` | [→]($HARNESS_REL/skills/clean-code/SKILL.md) |
| refactor | \`/refactor\` | [→]($HARNESS_REL/skills/refactor/SKILL.md) |
| review-comprehensive | \`/review-comprehensive\` | [→]($HARNESS_REL/skills/review-comprehensive/SKILL.md) |
| pr-interactive-walkthrough | \`/pr-interactive-walkthrough\` | [→]($HARNESS_REL/skills/pr-interactive-walkthrough/SKILL.md) |
| frontend-design | \`/frontend-design\` | [→]($HARNESS_REL/skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md) |
| systematic-debugging | \`/systematic-debugging\` | [→]($HARNESS_REL/skills/systematic-debugging/SKILL.md) |
| dispatching-parallel-agents | \`/dispatching-parallel-agents\` | [→]($HARNESS_REL/skills/dispatching-parallel-agents/SKILL.md) |
| skill-creator | \`/skill-creator\` | [→]($HARNESS_REL/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md) |
| btw-pull-request | \`/btw-pull-request\` | [→]($HARNESS_REL/skills/btw-pull-request/skill.md) |
EOF
  for s in "${REQUESTED_OPTIONAL[@]+"${REQUESTED_OPTIONAL[@]}"}"; do
    printf '| %s | \`/%s\` | [→](%s/skills/%s/SKILL.md) |\n' "$s" "$s" "$HARNESS_REL" "$s"
  done
}

workflow_block() {
  printf '```\n'
  cat <<'EOF'
/initialize     →  write or update context files in a target project
/problem-spec   →  define the problem, produce docs/<feature>/spec.md
/plan           →  break into TDD chunks, produce docs/<feature>/plan.md

  For each step:
    write tests (red) → write code (green) → refactor → commit
    /verify              →  E2E check against live system
    /clean-code          →  clean up staged code
    /review-comprehensive →  comprehensive correctness and edge case check
    /pr-interactive-walkthrough  →  cognitive understanding check
    human                →  sign off
EOF
  printf '```\n'
}

# write_context_file <path> <title>
write_context_file() {
  local file="$1"
  local title="$2"   # e.g. "AGENTS.md" or "CLAUDE.md"
  local nested_label="$title"

  cat > "$file" <<EOF
# $title

Read by Claude at the start of every session. Links to skill files rather than
duplicating them. For full instructions, read the linked SKILL.md.

---

<!-- nested-agents-index -->
<!-- nested-agents-index-end -->

---

## Workflow

For non-trivial features, follow this order:

$(workflow_block)

---

## Skills

$(skills_table)

---

## Behavioral Rules

Rules added when a pattern of mistakes recurs 3+ times.

<!-- learned-rules -->
<!-- learned-rules-end -->
EOF
}

# update_context_file <path> <label>
update_context_file() {
  local file="$1"
  local label="$2"
  local changed=false

  if ! grep -q '## Skills' "$file"; then
    printf '\n---\n\n## Skills\n\n%s\n' "$(skills_table)" >> "$file"
    green "  + added ## Skills"
    changed=true
  fi

  if ! grep -q '## Workflow' "$file"; then
    printf '\n---\n\n## Workflow\n\nFor non-trivial features, follow this order:\n\n%s\n' "$(workflow_block)" >> "$file"
    green "  + added ## Workflow"
    changed=true
  fi

  if ! grep -q 'nested-agents-index' "$file"; then
    printf '\n---\n\n## Nested %s\n\nCheck for %s in subdirectories before starting work in them.\n\n<!-- nested-agents-index -->\n<!-- nested-agents-index-end -->\n' "$label" "$label" >> "$file"
    green "  + added nested index"
    changed=true
  fi

  if ! grep -q 'learned-rules' "$file"; then
    printf '\n---\n\n## Behavioral Rules\n\nRules added when a pattern of mistakes recurs 3+ times.\n\n<!-- learned-rules -->\n<!-- learned-rules-end -->\n' >> "$file"
    green "  + added learned-rules block"
    changed=true
  fi

  if $changed; then
    green "Updated $file"
  else
    yellow "$file already complete — no changes"
  fi
}

# ── process each context file ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

printf '\n'
bold "Context files → $USER_CLAUDE_DIR"

for fname in AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md; do
  target_file="$USER_CLAUDE_DIR/$fname"
  if [[ ! -f "$target_file" ]]; then
    write_context_file "$target_file" "$fname"
    green "Created $target_file"
  else
    update_context_file "$target_file" "$fname"
  fi
done

# ── 3. hooks + settings ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Install the verify-evidence PostToolUse hook: it blocks marking a step verified
# unless the verify report shows real evidence (curl / Playwright / DB check).

printf '\n'
bold "Hooks → $USER_CLAUDE_DIR/hooks"

HOOKS_DST="$USER_CLAUDE_DIR/hooks"
mkdir -p "$HOOKS_DST"
cp "$HARNESS_DIR/hooks/verify-evidence.sh" "$HOOKS_DST/verify-evidence.sh"
chmod +x "$HOOKS_DST/verify-evidence.sh"
green "  + verify-evidence.sh"

SETTINGS="$USER_CLAUDE_DIR/settings.json"
HOOK_CMD="$HOOKS_DST/verify-evidence.sh"

if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then

    yellow "  settings.json already registers the verify-evidence hook — no change"
  else
    tmp="$(mktemp)"
    jq --arg c "$HOOK_CMD" '
      .hooks.PostToolUse = ((.hooks.PostToolUse // []) + [
        { matcher: "Skill", hooks: [ { type: "command", command: $c } ] }
      ])' "$SETTINGS" > "$tmp" && mv "$tmp" "$SETTINGS"
    green "  + registered verify-evidence PostToolUse hook in settings.json"

EOF

Skills and workflows for a standard agent development harness.

## Install

Run the install script once — it installs at the **user level** (`~/.claude`), so the skills
apply to every project automatically:

```

```bash
/path/to/harness/install.sh --dir <path>      # install into an alternate Claude dir (testing)
/path/to/harness/install.sh --with <skill>    # also install an optional skill (repeatable)
/path/to/harness/install.sh --with all        # install every optional skill

- Copy all skills into `~/.claude/skills/` (pruning any that no longer exist in the harness)
- Create `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` and `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, or add missing sections if they exist

## Claude Code Plugin Structure & Marketplace Guide

Based on official Claude Code documentation at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/, here's the exact structure and requirements for converting a skills repo into an installable plugin.

---

### 1. **Plugin Directory Structure**

A plugin is a self-contained directory. The critical rule: **only `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` goes inside `.claude-plugin/`**. Everything else (skills, agents, hooks, MCP, etc.) lives at the **plugin root**.

**Canonical layout:**
```
my-plugin/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json              ← ONLY plugin.json here
├── skills/
│   └── <skill-name>/
│       ├── SKILL.md             ← Required
│       ├── reference.md         ← Optional supporting files
│       └── scripts/             ← Optional supporting files
├── commands/                    ← Flat .md skill files (legacy)
├── agents/
│   └── agent-name.md
├── hooks/
│   └── hooks.json
├── .mcp.json                    ← MCP server configs
├── .lsp.json                    ← LSP server configs
├── monitors/
│   └── monitors.json
├── bin/                         ← Executables added to PATH
├── themes/                      ← Color theme definitions
├── output-styles/              ← Output style definitions
├── settings.json               ← Default plugin settings
└── README.md
```

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins.md (Plugin structure overview section)
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Plugin directory structure section)

---

### 2. **`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` Schema**

**Minimal required:**
```json
{
  "name": "my-plugin"
}
```

**Complete schema:**
```json
{
  "name": "plugin-name",
  "displayName": "Plugin Name",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "description": "Brief description",
  "author": {
    "name": "Your Name",
    "email": "you@example.com",
    "url": "https://github.com/you"
  },
  "homepage": "https://docs.example.com",
  "repository": "https://github.com/you/plugin",
  "license": "MIT",
  "keywords": ["keyword1"],
  "defaultEnabled": true,
  
  "skills": "./skills/",
  "commands": ["./commands/"],
  "agents": ["./agents/"],
  "hooks": "./hooks/hooks.json",
  "mcpServers": "./.mcp.json",
  "lspServers": "./.lsp.json",
  "outputStyles": "./output-styles/",
  
  "experimental": {
    "themes": "./themes/",
    "monitors": "./monitors.json"
  },
  
  "dependencies": [
    "helper-plugin",
    { "name": "other-plugin", "version": "~2.1.0" }
  ]
}
```

**Key fields:**
- `name` (required): kebab-case, unique identifier. Becomes skill namespace: `/name:skill-name`
- `displayName` (optional): human-readable UI name with spaces (v2.1.143+)
- `version` (optional): semantic version. Omit to auto-use git commit SHA (every commit = new version)
- `defaultEnabled` (optional): whether enabled by default on install (v2.1.154+)

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Plugin manifest schema section)

---

### 3. **Skills in Plugins**

**Directory structure (preferred for multi-skill plugins):**
```
skills/
├── skill-one/
│   ├── SKILL.md              ← Required
│   ├── helpers.py            ← Optional supporting files
│   └── reference.md
└── skill-two/
    └── SKILL.md
```

**Single-skill shortcut:** If a plugin has no `skills/` dir and no `skills` manifest field, a `SKILL.md` at the plugin root is loaded as a single skill.

**SKILL.md frontmatter & format:**
```markdown
---
name: optional-skill-name
description: Describes what the skill does. Claude uses this to decide when to invoke it.
disable-model-invocation: false
---

# Optional heading

Detailed instructions for Claude about how to use this skill.
Include context, examples, and any constraints.

You can reference ${ARGUMENTS} for user input.
```

**Frontmatter fields:**
- `description` (required): Claude uses this to auto-invoke skills; also shown in UI
- `name` (optional): overrides directory name for invocation
- `disable-model-invocation` (optional): if `true`, Claude never auto-invokes; only user-triggered

Skills in plugins are namespaced: a skill named `hello` in plugin `my-plugin` is invoked as `/my-plugin:hello`.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins.md (Add Skills to your plugin section)
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Skills section)

---

### 4. **Path Variables & Conventions**

**Available in hooks, MCP/LSP configs, monitor commands, and skill content:**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "my-server": {
      "command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/servers/my-server",
      "args": ["--config", "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/config.json"],
      "env": {
        "DATA_PATH": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- **`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`**: absolute path to plugin's installation directory. Use for scripts, binaries, config. Changes on updates. In shell commands, wrap in double quotes: `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"`
- **`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`**: persistent directory (survives plugin updates) at `~/.claude/plugins/data/{plugin-id}/`. Use for state, dependencies, caches.
- **`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`**: project root. Use for project-local scripts.

All paths are also exported as env vars to MCP/LSP subprocesses.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Environment variables section)

---

### 5. **Hooks in Plugins**

**Location:** `hooks/hooks.json` in plugin root (or inline in `plugin.json`)

**Schema:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Write|Edit",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "\"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}\"/scripts/format.sh"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "SessionStart": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "\"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}\"/scripts/init.sh"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Hook types:** `command`, `http`, `mcp_tool`, `prompt`, `agent`

**Key events:** `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `SessionEnd`, `PermissionRequest`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, etc. (15+ total)

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Hooks section)

---

### 6. **Plugin Marketplace Schema** (`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`)

A marketplace is a catalog file that lists plugins and where to fetch them.

**Location:** `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at marketplace root

**Schema:**
```json
{
  "name": "my-plugins",
  "description": "Team plugin catalog",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "owner": {
    "name": "Your Name",
    "email": "you@example.com"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "pluginRoot": "./plugins"
  },
  "allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn": [
    "other-marketplace-name"
  ],
  "renames": {
    "old-plugin-name": "new-plugin-name",
    "removed-plugin": null
  },
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "formatter",
      "displayName": "Code Formatter",
      "source": "./plugins/formatter",
      "description": "Automatic code formatting",
      "version": "1.0.0",
      "author": { "name": "Team" },
      "homepage": "https://docs.example.com",
      "repository": "https://github.com/you/formatter",
      "license": "MIT",
      "keywords": ["formatting"],
      "category": "productivity",
      "tags": ["code-quality"],
      "defaultEnabled": true,
      "strict": true
    },
    {
      "name": "github-tools",
      "source": {
        "source": "github",
        "repo": "owner/repo-name",
        "ref": "v2.0.0",
        "sha": "a1b2c3d4..."
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "external-plugin",
      "source": {
        "source": "url",
        "url": "https://gitlab.com/team/plugin.git",
        "ref": "main"
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "monorepo-plugin",
      "source": {
        "source": "git-subdir",
        "url": "https://github.com/org/mono.git",
        "path": "tools/claude-plugin"
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "npm-plugin",
      "source": {
        "source": "npm",
        "package": "@org/plugin",
        "version": "^2.0.0",
        "registry": "https://npm.example.com"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

**Marketplace-level required fields:**
- `name` (string): marketplace identifier (kebab-case)
- `owner` (object): `{name, email?}`
- `plugins` (array): list of plugins

**Plugin entry required fields:**
- `name` (string): plugin identifier (kebab-case)
- `source` (string|object): where to fetch the plugin

**Plugin source types:**
- **Relative path:** `"./plugins/my-plugin"` (resolves relative to marketplace root)
- **GitHub:** `{"source": "github", "repo": "owner/repo", "ref"?: "v1.0", "sha"?: "abc..."}`
- **Git URL:** `{"source": "url", "url": "https://gitlab.com/...", "ref"?: "main", "sha"?: "abc..."}`
- **Git subdirectory:** `{"source": "git-subdir", "url": "...", "path": "tools/plugin", "ref"?: "...", "sha"?: "..."}`
- **npm:** `{"source": "npm", "package": "@org/plugin", "version"?: "^2.0", "registry"?: "https://..."}`

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces.md (Marketplace schema & Plugin entries sections)

---

### 7. **Plugin vs Standalone Configuration**

| Aspect | Standalone (`.claude/`) | Plugin |
|--------|-------------------------|--------|
| **Skill names** | `/hello` | `/plugin-name:hello` |
| **Scope** | Single project | Shared via marketplace |
| **Discovery** | Auto-discovered in `.claude/` | Installed from marketplace |
| **Versioning** | Git-tracked | Marketplace + version control |
| **Distribution** | Manual copy | `/plugin install <name>` |
| **Best for** | Project-specific, personal | Team, community, reusable |

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins.md (When to use plugins vs standalone configuration section)

---

### 8. **How Users Install & Use**

**Add a marketplace:**
```bash
/plugin marketplace add owner/repo              # GitHub shorthand
/plugin marketplace add https://gitlab.com/..   # Git URL
/plugin marketplace add ./local/path            # Local directory
/plugin marketplace add https://example.com/marketplace.json  # URL to file
```

**Install a plugin:**
```bash
/plugin install plugin-name@marketplace-name    # Interactive scope choice
claude plugin install plugin-name@marketplace-name --scope project
```

**Manage plugins:**
```bash
/plugin                      # Open UI
/plugin list                 # List installed
/plugin details name         # Show components & cost
/plugin disable name         # Disable without uninstalling
/plugin update name          # Update to latest
/plugin uninstall name       # Remove
/reload-plugins              # Reload after changes
```

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins.md (Add marketplaces & Install plugins sections)
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (CLI commands reference)

---

### 9. **Agents in Plugins**

**Location:** `agents/` directory in plugin root

**File format:** Markdown with YAML frontmatter

```markdown
---
name: code-reviewer
description: Reviews code for bugs, security, and performance
model: sonnet
effort: medium
maxTurns: 20
skills: []
disallowedTools: ["Write"]
---

You are an expert code reviewer. Focus on:
- Correctness and edge cases
- Security vulnerabilities
- Performance optimizations
- Code clarity and maintainability
```

**Frontmatter fields:** `name`, `description`, `model`, `effort`, `maxTurns`, `skills`, `disallowedTools`, `memory`, `background`, `isolation` ("worktree" only)

Agents appear as `plugin-name:agent-name` in @-mention typeahead.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Agents section)

---

### 10. **MCP & LSP Servers in Plugins**

**MCP servers** (`.mcp.json` or inline in `plugin.json`):
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "database": {
      "command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/servers/db-server",
      "args": ["--config", "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/config.json"],
      "env": { "DB_PATH": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}" }
    }
  }
}
```

**LSP servers** (`.lsp.json` or inline):
```json
{
  "go": {
    "command": "gopls",
    "args": ["serve"],
    "extensionToLanguage": { ".go": "go" }
  }
}
```

Both start automatically when plugin is enabled.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (MCP servers & LSP servers sections)

---

### 11. **Version Management & Release Channels**

**Two approaches:**

1. **Explicit version** (published plugins):
   - Set `"version": "2.1.0"` in `plugin.json`
   - Users get updates only when you bump this field
   - Must follow semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH)
   - Document in `CHANGELOG.md`

2. **Commit-SHA version** (actively developed plugins):
   - Omit `version` from both `plugin.json` and marketplace entry
   - Every new commit = new version
   - Best for internal/team plugins

If `version` is set in both `plugin.json` and marketplace entry, `plugin.json` wins.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces.md (Version resolution and release channels section)
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Version management section)

---

### 12. **Marketplace Distribution Methods**

| Host | Add command | Setup |
|------|-------------|-------|
| **GitHub** (recommended) | `/plugin marketplace add owner/repo` | Create `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` in repo root; users clone via git |
| **Other Git** (GitLab, etc.) | `/plugin marketplace add https://gitlab.com/team/plugins.git` | Any git host with `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` |
| **Local development** | `/plugin marketplace add ./path/to/marketplace` | Directory with `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` |
| **Remote URL** | `/plugin marketplace add https://example.com/marketplace.json` | Direct URL to file (limitations: relative plugin paths won't work) |
| **npm** | plugins shipped as npm packages | `source: { "source": "npm", "package": "@org/plugin" }` |

**Private repositories:** Use git credential helpers (GitHub, GitLab tokens in environment for auto-updates)

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces.md (Host and distribute marketplaces section)

---

### 13. **File Caching & Path Traversal**

Marketplace plugins are **copied** to `~/.claude/plugins/cache/{marketplace}/{plugin}/{version}/` on install.

**Critical limitation:** Plugins cannot reference files outside their directory.
- ✅ Good: `./scripts/run.sh`
- ❌ Bad: `../shared-utils/helper.py` (not copied)

**Workaround:** Use symlinks inside the plugin directory. Symlinks to other plugins in same marketplace are dereferenced (content copied).

Example: Link to shared skill in another plugin:
```bash
ln -s ../../shared-plugin/skills/foo ./skills/foo
```

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Plugin caching and file resolution section)

---

### 14. **Skills-Directory Plugins** (Auto-loaded, no marketplace)

Any folder under `~/.claude/skills/` or `.claude/skills/` with a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` loads automatically as `{name}@skills-dir` on next session.

**Scaffold one:**
```bash
claude plugin init my-helper
```

Project-scope (`.claude/skills/`) plugins load only after workspace trust. Personal-scope (`~/.claude/skills/`) have no restrictions.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Skills-directory plugins section)

---

### 15. **Plugin Validation & Testing**

```bash
claude plugin validate ./my-plugin
/plugin validate ./my-plugin
```

**Checks:**
- JSON syntax in `plugin.json`, `hooks.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.lsp.json`
- Duplicate plugin names
- YAML frontmatter in SKILL.md, agents, commands
- Source path validation (no `..` traversal)
- Component discovery

Use `--strict` to treat warnings as errors (recommended for CI).

**Test locally:**
```bash
claude --plugin-dir ./my-plugin
/plugin marketplace add ./local/marketplace
/plugin install plugin-name@local-marketplace

## Claude Code Plugin Structure & Marketplace Guide

Based on official Claude Code documentation at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/, here's the exact structure and requirements for converting a skills repo into an installable plugin.

---

### 1. **Plugin Directory Structure**

A plugin is a self-contained directory. The critical rule: **only `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` goes inside `.claude-plugin/`**. Everything else (skills, agents, hooks, MCP, etc.) lives at the **plugin root**.

**Canonical layout:**
```
my-plugin/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json              ← ONLY plugin.json here
├── skills/
│   └── <skill-name>/
│       ├── SKILL.md             ← Required
│       ├── reference.md         ← Optional supporting files
│       └── scripts/             ← Optional supporting files
├── commands/                    ← Flat .md skill files (legacy)
├── agents/
│   └── agent-name.md
├── hooks/
│   └── hooks.json
├── .mcp.json                    ← MCP server configs
├── .lsp.json                    ← LSP server configs
├── monitors/
│   └── monitors.json
├── bin/                         ← Executables added to PATH
├── themes/                      ← Color theme definitions
├── output-styles/              ← Output style definitions
├── settings.json               ← Default plugin settings
└── README.md
```

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins.md (Plugin structure overview section)
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Plugin directory structure section)

---

### 2. **`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` Schema**

**Minimal required:**
```json
{
  "name": "my-plugin"
}
```

**Complete schema:**
```json
{
  "name": "plugin-name",
  "displayName": "Plugin Name",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "description": "Brief description",
  "author": {
    "name": "Your Name",
    "email": "you@example.com",
    "url": "https://github.com/you"
  },
  "homepage": "https://docs.example.com",
  "repository": "https://github.com/you/plugin",
  "license": "MIT",
  "keywords": ["keyword1"],
  "defaultEnabled": true,
  
  "skills": "./skills/",
  "commands": ["./commands/"],
  "agents": ["./agents/"],
  "hooks": "./hooks/hooks.json",
  "mcpServers": "./.mcp.json",
  "lspServers": "./.lsp.json",
  "outputStyles": "./output-styles/",
  
  "experimental": {
    "themes": "./themes/",
    "monitors": "./monitors.json"
  },
  
  "dependencies": [
    "helper-plugin",
    { "name": "other-plugin", "version": "~2.1.0" }
  ]
}
```

**Key fields:**
- `name` (required): kebab-case, unique identifier. Becomes skill namespace: `/name:skill-name`
- `displayName` (optional): human-readable UI name with spaces (v2.1.143+)
- `version` (optional): semantic version. Omit to auto-use git commit SHA (every commit = new version)
- `defaultEnabled` (optional): whether enabled by default on install (v2.1.154+)

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Plugin manifest schema section)

---

### 3. **Skills in Plugins**

**Directory structure (preferred for multi-skill plugins):**
```
skills/
├── skill-one/
│   ├── SKILL.md              ← Required
│   ├── helpers.py            ← Optional supporting files
│   └── reference.md
└── skill-two/
    └── SKILL.md
```

**Single-skill shortcut:** If a plugin has no `skills/` dir and no `skills` manifest field, a `SKILL.md` at the plugin root is loaded as a single skill.

**SKILL.md frontmatter & format:**
```markdown
---
name: optional-skill-name
description: Describes what the skill does. Claude uses this to decide when to invoke it.
disable-model-invocation: false
---

# Optional heading

Detailed instructions for Claude about how to use this skill.
Include context, examples, and any constraints.

You can reference ${ARGUMENTS} for user input.
```

**Frontmatter fields:**
- `description` (required): Claude uses this to auto-invoke skills; also shown in UI
- `name` (optional): overrides directory name for invocation
- `disable-model-invocation` (optional): if `true`, Claude never auto-invokes; only user-triggered

Skills in plugins are namespaced: a skill named `hello` in plugin `my-plugin` is invoked as `/my-plugin:hello`.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins.md (Add Skills to your plugin section)
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Skills section)

### 4. **Path Variables & Conventions**

**Available in hooks, MCP/LSP configs, monitor commands, and skill content:**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "my-server": {
      "command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/servers/my-server",
      "args": ["--config", "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/config.json"],
      "env": {
        "DATA_PATH": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- **`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`**: absolute path to plugin's installation directory. Use for scripts, binaries, config. Changes on updates. In shell commands, wrap in double quotes: `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"`
- **`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`**: persistent directory (survives plugin updates) at `~/.claude/plugins/data/{plugin-id}/`. Use for state, dependencies, caches.
- **`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`**: project root. Use for project-local scripts.

All paths are also exported as env vars to MCP/LSP subprocesses.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Environment variables section)

---

### 5. **Hooks in Plugins**

**Location:** `hooks/hooks.json` in plugin root (or inline in `plugin.json`)

**Schema:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Write|Edit",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "\"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}\"/scripts/format.sh"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "SessionStart": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "\"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}\"/scripts/init.sh"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Hook types:** `command`, `http`, `mcp_tool`, `prompt`, `agent`

**Key events:** `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `SessionEnd`, `PermissionRequest`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, etc. (15+ total)

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Hooks section)

---

### 6. **Plugin Marketplace Schema** (`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`)

A marketplace is a catalog file that lists plugins and where to fetch them.

**Location:** `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at marketplace root

**Schema:**
```json
{
  "name": "my-plugins",
  "description": "Team plugin catalog",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "owner": {
    "name": "Your Name",
    "email": "you@example.com"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "pluginRoot": "./plugins"
  },
  "allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn": [
    "other-marketplace-name"
  ],
  "renames": {
    "old-plugin-name": "new-plugin-name",
    "removed-plugin": null
  },
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "formatter",
      "displayName": "Code Formatter",
      "source": "./plugins/formatter",
      "description": "Automatic code formatting",
      "version": "1.0.0",
      "author": { "name": "Team" },
      "homepage": "https://docs.example.com",
      "repository": "https://github.com/you/formatter",
      "license": "MIT",
      "keywords": ["formatting"],
      "category": "productivity",
      "tags": ["code-quality"],
      "defaultEnabled": true,
      "strict": true
    },
    {
      "name": "github-tools",
      "source": {
        "source": "github",
        "repo": "owner/repo-name",
        "ref": "v2.0.0",
        "sha": "a1b2c3d4..."
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "external-plugin",
      "source": {
        "source": "url",
        "url": "https://gitlab.com/team/plugin.git",
        "ref": "main"
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "monorepo-plugin",
      "source": {
        "source": "git-subdir",
        "url": "https://github.com/org/mono.git",
        "path": "tools/claude-plugin"
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "npm-plugin",
      "source": {
        "source": "npm",
        "package": "@org/plugin",
        "version": "^2.0.0",
        "registry": "https://npm.example.com"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

**Marketplace-level required fields:**
- `name` (string): marketplace identifier (kebab-case)
- `owner` (object): `{name, email?}`
- `plugins` (array): list of plugins

**Plugin entry required fields:**
- `name` (string): plugin identifier (kebab-case)
- `source` (string|object): where to fetch the plugin

**Plugin source types:**
- **Relative path:** `"./plugins/my-plugin"` (resolves relative to marketplace root)
- **GitHub:** `{"source": "github", "repo": "owner/repo", "ref"?: "v1.0", "sha"?: "abc..."}`
- **Git URL:** `{"source": "url", "url": "https://gitlab.com/...", "ref"?: "main", "sha"?: "abc..."}`
- **Git subdirectory:** `{"source": "git-subdir", "url": "...", "path": "tools/plugin", "ref"?: "...", "sha"?: "..."}`
- **npm:** `{"source": "npm", "package": "@org/plugin", "version"?: "^2.0", "registry"?: "https://..."}`

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces.md (Marketplace schema & Plugin entries sections)

### 7. **Plugin vs Standalone Configuration**

| Aspect | Standalone (`.claude/`) | Plugin |
|--------|-------------------------|--------|
| **Skill names** | `/hello` | `/plugin-name:hello` |
| **Scope** | Single project | Shared via marketplace |
| **Discovery** | Auto-discovered in `.claude/` | Installed from marketplace |
| **Versioning** | Git-tracked | Marketplace + version control |
| **Distribution** | Manual copy | `/plugin install <name>` |
| **Best for** | Project-specific, personal | Team, community, reusable |

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins.md (When to use plugins vs standalone configuration section)

### 8. **How Users Install & Use**

**Add a marketplace:**
```bash
/plugin marketplace add owner/repo              # GitHub shorthand
/plugin marketplace add https://gitlab.com/..   # Git URL
/plugin marketplace add ./local/path            # Local directory
/plugin marketplace add https://example.com/marketplace.json  # URL to file
```

**Install a plugin:**
```bash
/plugin install plugin-name@marketplace-name    # Interactive scope choice
claude plugin install plugin-name@marketplace-name --scope project
```

**Manage plugins:**
```bash
/plugin                      # Open UI
/plugin list                 # List installed
/plugin details name         # Show components & cost
/plugin disable name         # Disable without uninstalling
/plugin update name          # Update to latest
/plugin uninstall name       # Remove
/reload-plugins              # Reload after changes
```

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins.md (Add marketplaces & Install plugins sections)
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (CLI commands reference)

---
name: code-reviewer
description: Reviews code for bugs, security, and performance
model: sonnet
effort: medium
maxTurns: 20
skills: []
disallowedTools: ["Write"]
---

You are an expert code reviewer. Focus on:
- Correctness and edge cases
- Security vulnerabilities
- Performance optimizations
- Code clarity and maintainability
```

**Frontmatter fields:** `name`, `description`, `model`, `effort`, `maxTurns`, `skills`, `disallowedTools`, `memory`, `background`, `isolation` ("worktree" only)

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Agents section)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "database": {
      "command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/servers/db-server",
      "args": ["--config", "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/config.json"],
      "env": { "DB_PATH": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}" }
    }
  }

```json

    "command": "gopls",
    "args": ["serve"],
    "extensionToLanguage": { ".go": "go" }
  }
}
```

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (MCP servers & LSP servers sections)

### 11. **Version Management & Release Channels**

**Two approaches:**

1. **Explicit version** (published plugins):
   - Set `"version": "2.1.0"` in `plugin.json`
   - Users get updates only when you bump this field
   - Must follow semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH)
   - Document in `CHANGELOG.md`

2. **Commit-SHA version** (actively developed plugins):
   - Omit `version` from both `plugin.json` and marketplace entry
   - Every new commit = new version
   - Best for internal/team plugins

If `version` is set in both `plugin.json` and marketplace entry, `plugin.json` wins.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces.md (Version resolution and release channels section)
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Version management section)

| Host | Add command | Setup |
|------|-------------|-------|
| **GitHub** (recommended) | `/plugin marketplace add owner/repo` | Create `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` in repo root; users clone via git |

| **Remote URL** | `/plugin marketplace add https://example.com/marketplace.json` | Direct URL to file (limitations: relative plugin paths won't work) |
| **npm** | plugins shipped as npm packages | `source: { "source": "npm", "package": "@org/plugin" }` |

**Private repositories:** Use git credential helpers (GitHub, GitLab tokens in environment for auto-updates)

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces.md (Host and distribute marketplaces section)

### 13. **File Caching & Path Traversal**

Marketplace plugins are **copied** to `~/.claude/plugins/cache/{marketplace}/{plugin}/{version}/` on install.

**Critical limitation:** Plugins cannot reference files outside their directory.
- ✅ Good: `./scripts/run.sh`
- ❌ Bad: `../shared-utils/helper.py` (not copied)

**Workaround:** Use symlinks inside the plugin directory. Symlinks to other plugins in same marketplace are dereferenced (content copied).

Example: Link to shared skill in another plugin:
```bash
ln -s ../../shared-plugin/skills/foo ./skills/foo
```

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Plugin caching and file resolution section)

### 14. **Skills-Directory Plugins** (Auto-loaded, no marketplace)

Any folder under `~/.claude/skills/` or `.claude/skills/` with a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` loads automatically as `{name}@skills-dir` on next session.

**Scaffold one:**
```bash
claude plugin init my-helper

Project-scope (`.claude/skills/`) plugins load only after workspace trust. Personal-scope (`~/.claude/skills/`) have no restrictions.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Skills-directory plugins section)

claude plugin validate ./my-plugin
/plugin validate ./my-plugin

- JSON syntax in `plugin.json`, `hooks.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.lsp.json`
- Duplicate plugin names
- YAML frontmatter in SKILL.md, agents, commands
- Source path validation (no `..` traversal)
- Component discovery

Use `--strict` to treat warnings as errors (recommended for CI).

**Test locally:**
```bash
claude --plugin-dir ./my-plugin
/plugin marketplace add ./local/marketplace
/plugin install plugin-name@local-marketplace
```
